AuditTemplate.description:
A named set of audit columns applied during data shaping.

A template is written either nested under ``columns`` or as a flat mapping
of column names to expressions. A mapping with a ``columns`` key is read as
the nested form, so a flat template cannot define a column named
``columns``.

Attributes:
    columns: Mapping of column names to Spark SQL expressions. Each entry
        defines a column that will be appended to the output dataset.

Example:
    >>> template = AuditTemplate(
    ...     columns={
    ...         "created_at": "current_timestamp()",
    ...         "created_by": "current_user()",
    ...     }
    ... )
    >>> AuditTemplate.model_validate({"created_at": "current_timestamp()"}).columns
    {'created_at': 'current_timestamp()'}

RunStore.description:
Where runs write their output, and in which layout.

Every field applies to both layouts: ``connection`` moves the store's
base in either, and ``schema`` names the shared schema or overrides the
per-project one.

connection.description: Name of the connection whose lakehouse holds the run store.
connection.title: Connection

layout.description: 'per_project' gives the project its own tables; 'shared' writes to one schema that several projects share, each row carrying its project_id.
layout.title: Layout

schema.description: Schema name. shared: the shared schema (default 'weevr'); per_project: overrides the name derived from the project name.
schema.title: Schema

description:
A project's root document, ``weevr.yaml``.

Identifies the project, optionally pins the weevr versions it runs on,
says where its run store is, and declares what every config in the
project sees. Its ``params`` are the outermost tier of the spec cascade:
runtime params bind over their defaults, and a loom, weave or thread
declaring the same name shadows them. Its ``connections``,
``audit_templates`` and ``defaults`` are the outermost tier of the load
cascade, in the shapes a loom declares them: connections and audit
templates merge by name (the nearest declaration wins), and a lower
``defaults:`` block replaces the project's key by key. ``variables`` is
reserved and rejected at load.

kind.description: Document kind. A project document declares 'project'.
kind.title: Kind

id.description: The project's GUID, generated once and never derived from Fabric IDs.
id.title: Id

name.description: Project name; also the default run-store schema suffix, so it must be a schema-safe identifier.
name.title: Name

requires_weevr.description: PEP 440 version specifier the installed weevr must satisfy (e.g. '>=2,<3').
requires_weevr.title: Requires Weevr

run_store.description: Run-store settings; omitted means the container's default.

params.description: Typed parameter declarations every loom, weave and thread in the project sees; a declaration of the same name in a document shadows the project's.
params.title: Params

strict_params.description: Enforce the params contract project-wide: a ${param.x} reference must be declared (P120) and every runtime param declared or referenced (P121). A document's own strict_params, or the load's, overrides it; unset is lenient.
strict_params.title: Strict Params

defaults.description: Default values inherited by every loom, weave and thread in the project; a lower tier's defaults block replaces a key the project sets.
defaults.title: Defaults

audit_templates.description: Named audit column templates every loom, weave and thread in the project sees; a template of the same name declared lower down shadows the project's.
audit_templates.title: Audit Templates

connections.description: Named connection definitions every loom, weave and thread in the project sees; a connection of the same name declared lower down shadows the project's.
connections.title: Connections
